I'm an old man now, 71 years, but I've farmed this land for 55 years. My wife and I work together — our children are grown and gone. Five mu isn't much, but at our age it's what we can handle. Let me think through this year.

Most of my land, about 4 mu, I'll do the wheat-maize like always. It's what this land is for. The other 1 mu I keep in cotton — my neighbor老王 always does cotton too, and it gives us some cash money even though the picking is hard on my back. I hire my nephew's wife and some village women to help at picking time.

For wheat, I planted already in October — I always plant around National Day time, when the neighbors plant. Used hybrid seed from the agricultural supply shop in town, about one bag and a half per mu. Before planting I spread two bags of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) per mu and plowed it in. When it warms up in March I'll topdress urea, maybe one bag per mu, and irrigate. I always irrigate three times — before winter, at greening, and at jointing. Water from the well costs money but wheat needs it. I hope for 400 kg/mu, same as last year.

Maize goes in right after wheat harvest in June — that week is crazy busy, I hire the combine harvester and planter together from the village cooperative, no time to do it myself. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan or similar, whatever the seed shop recommends. Put down compound fertilizer at planting, topdress urea at big喇叭口 stage. If it rains enough I don't irrigate, but usually I water once at tasseling. Expect 450 kg/mu.

Cotton is more trouble. Plant in late April after plowing. I use Bt cotton seed — we've used it for many years now, the bollworm problem is much less. Apply base fertilizer, then topdress at flowering. Spray for aphids and mites a few times. Pick by hand in September and October — three or four pickings. That's when I need the hired help, my hands aren't what they used to be.

Money is tight. I don't buy more fertilizer than I need. If the crop looks yellow I add a little, if it looks good I save the money. My neighbor sometimes uses less and still gets good yield, so I don't overdo it.
